Period: 21 Nov 2021 to 18 Oct 2026 (257 weeks). Both series are public and aggregate, so no personal data and no POPIA consent issue. | | Methods used | Student-$t$ GARCH(1,1) with a lagged search term in the variance equation (GARCH-X), estimated by constrained quasi-maximum likelihood. GJR-GARCH and EGARCH benchmarks. Boundary-corrected likelihood-ratio test. Out-of-sample QLIKE against realised variance (HAC and block-bootstrap tests). Granger tests with Holm correction. Monte Carlo power study. | ::: ## Question Does South African search interest in the rand carry information about next-week ZAR/USD volatility beyond what past returns already contain? ## Key findings
6.559
attention coefficient (estimate)
<0.001
in-sample p-value (boundary-corrected LR)
0.001

not reached
smallest effect detected with 80% power
- **In sample.** The estimated coefficient is $\hat\delta =$ 6.559 (robust t-ratio from the cross-check fit: 0.00). The boundary-corrected likelihood-ratio test rejects the null of no attention effect at the 5% level. A sustained move in attention from its minimum to its maximum changes long-run variance by about 182.2%. - **Out of sample.** Across 103 expanding-window forecasts, the mean QLIKE gain of GARCH-X over GARCH is 0.153 (positive favours GARCH-X). The HAC p-value is 0.001 and the block-bootstrap p-value is NA. - **Direction.** The smallest Holm-adjusted Granger p-value is <0.001 for search leading volatility and <0.001 for volatility leading search. - **Power.** The test's empirical size is 39%, and it needs an effect of about not reached to reach 80% power. A non-rejection therefore rules out only large effects. **What this does and does not show.** The results speak to predictive association at weekly frequency. They do not show that searches cause volatility, because attention, trading and news can all move together. ![Left: cumulative out-of-sample QLIKE gain of GARCH-X over GARCH. Right: power of the boundary-corrected likelihood-ratio test, with the observed effect marked.](figures/p1_headline.png){fig-alt="Two panels: cumulative forecast gain of GARCH-X over GARCH, and the power curve of the likelihood-ratio test."} ## What I would do differently I would pair daily returns with a MIDAS-style specification instead of aggregating to weeks, and extend the panel to several emerging-market currencies with local search terms to get past the five-year weekly Trends window. I would replace the asymptotic tests with a block bootstrap throughout, and I would fix the search term, lag and loss function in writing before touching the data, which I only partly did here. ## Detailed analysis [Read the detailed analysis →](analysis.html){.pf-button} Code and data: [Code & Data appendix](../../appendix/code_and_data.qmd).
